basis.text: Greene's report of 12 July 1863 (ten days after) is the only clock reading for the attack on the works by a man who was attacked: a few minutes before 7 p. m.; the Confederate reports give an advance about 6, dusk and dark, which are an earlier approach and later periods.

default.label: About 19:00 on Jul 2: Johnson's division attacks Greene on Culp's Hill
default.note: Greene's 'a few minutes before 7 p. m.' is the instant the first charge reaches his works; the Confederate advance from their line began earlier (about 18:00) and the fighting went on to 9.30.

positions.label: About 19:00: Greene's brigade is attacked a few minutes before 7 p. m. (Greene's report)

support.quote: Before any further movements could be made, we were attacked on the whole of our front by a large force a few minutes before 7 p. m. The enemy made four distinct charges between 7 and 9.30 p. m.

witness.name: George S. Greene
witness.role: Brigadier General, commanding the Third Brigade, 2nd Division, XII Corps (alone on Culp's Hill)

support.note: Greene, report of 12 July 1863 (ten days after), the brigadier whose line was attacked: after the First Division and two brigades of the Second left his right at 6.30 p. m., he had begun to occupy the empty works, and "Before any further movements could be made, we were attacked on the whole of our front by a large force a few minutes before 7 p. m." Four charges followed between 7 and 9.30. The only clock reading for the attack on the works by a man who was attacked.

support.quote: Johnson's division, of Ewell's corps, which attacked us on the night of the 2d instant

witness.name: George S. Greene
witness.role: Brigadier General, commanding the Third Brigade, 2nd Division, XII Corps (alone on Culp's Hill)

support.note: Greene, same report: the force that attacked his brigade was Johnson's division of Ewell's corps, "on the night of the 2d instant" (the day atom of the value).

support.quote: sustaining their desperate position during an incessant attack of two and a half hours

witness.name: John W. Geary
witness.role: Brigadier General, commanding the 2nd Division, XII Corps

support.note: Geary, report of 29 July 1863: Greene's brigade sustained "an incessant attack of two and a half hours" against four charges. Counted back from Greene's end of the firing at 9.30, two and a half hours begins at 7. Geary was away with the First and Second Brigades and writes of what he learned.

positions.label: About 19:30: Geary's order to hold the creek is at 7.30 and Greene is attacked in the meantime; Ewell has dusk

inference.step: Geary dates his order to hold the creek at 7.30 and puts Greene's attack "in the meantime", read as at or after 19:30; Ewell has the attack about dusk, after the guns stopped just before sundown, and the plan's computed sunset is 19:32. Read together, about 19:30; no writer gives 19:30 for the attack itself.

reason_not_chosen.text: Geary was marching away and gives only a sequence, and Ewell was behind the line and gives dusk, a period; Greene, who was attacked, gives a clock reading.

support.quote: At 7.30 o'clock I received an order to hold the position down to the creek at all hazards [...] In the meantime General Greene had commenced to extend his brigade, as ordered, along the line of intrenchments, and had barely occupied General Kane's original position when a vigorous attack was made upon his front and right by the enemy

witness.name: John W. Geary
witness.role: Brigadier General, commanding the 2nd Division, XII Corps

support.note: Geary, report of 29 July 1863 (27 days after), at the bridge on the turnpike with two brigades: at 7.30 he received the order to hold the creek, "In the meantime" Greene had barely occupied Kane's position "when a vigorous attack was made". He was elsewhere; "in the meantime" gives a sequence, not an hour for the attack, and the attack is no later than his writing.

support.page_note: the article begins on page 317 by the contents list of the volume; the OCR text has no page heads near the passage, so the printed page was not read
support.quote: The rest of the corps moved off just before dusk (about 7 P. M.)

witness.name: George S. Greene
witness.role: Brigadier General, commanding the Third Brigade, 2nd Division, XII Corps (alone on Culp's Hill)

support.note: Greene, Battles and Leaders (1887, 24 years after): the rest of the corps moved off "just before dusk (about 7 P. M.)", and his brigade was attacked as it extended to the right. In his report of 1863 the other troops left at 6.30; the two accounts of one man put the departure at 6.30 and about 7 and the attack just before and just after.

support.page_note: printed page read from the running head in the text (the head of page 447 stands before the passage)
support.quote: just before sundown, General Johnson ordered forward his division to attack [...] wooded hill in [...] front, and about dusk [...] attack was made

witness.name: Richard S. Ewell
witness.role: Lieutenant General, commanding the Second Corps

support.note: Ewell, report of the Second Corps (the printed date line gives the year 1863 and leaves month and day blank; the year is all the print gives): immediately after the artillery fire ceased, "which was just before sundown", Johnson ordered his division forward "and about dusk the attack was made". Ewell was behind the line and relays.

positions.label: About 18:00: the 21st Virginia advances from its line (Moseley); Steuart's brigade moves shortly after 5

reason_not_chosen.text: This is the advance from the line of battle across Rock Creek and up the mountain, which took an hour; Greene dates the attack on his works a few minutes before 7.

witness.name: W. P. Moseley
witness.role: Captain, commanding the 21st Virginia (Jones's brigade, Johnson's division)

support.note: Moseley, report of 21 July 1863 (19 days after), the captain commanding the 21st Virginia: the regiment "remained in that position until about 6 p. m. of the 2d, when it advanced against the enemy, intrenched on the mountain in its front"; it fell back about 8 o'clock. The advance across the valley, not the contact with the works.

support.quote: were relieved at about 5 o'clock by four companies of skirmishers from the Twenty- third Virginia, and shortly afterward the brigade was formed in line of battle and moved forward

witness.name: George H. Steuart
witness.role: Brigadier General, commanding a brigade of Johnson's division

support.note: Steuart, report of 2 September 1863 (62 days after): his pickets were relieved at about 5 o'clock by four companies of skirmishers from the 23rd Virginia, and "shortly afterward the brigade was formed in line of battle and moved forward". No hour for the contact.

reason_not_chosen.text: "Dusk" and "dark" are periods, not clock readings, and by the plan's computed sunset (19:32) they begin about half an hour after Greene's a few minutes before 7.

positions.label: About 20:00: the 21st Virginia falls back; Greene's right flank is turned (Moseley, Greene)

reason_not_chosen.text: Both are later events of the fight, not its start: the first attack of one regiment ending and the flank attack on Greene's right.

support.quote: remained in that position until about 6 p. m. of the 2d, when it advanced against the enemy, intrenched on the mountain in its front. The advance did not prove successful, and the regiment fell back about 8 o'clock to the branch at the foot of the mountain

witness.name: W. P. Moseley
witness.role: Captain, commanding the 21st Virginia (Jones's brigade, Johnson's division)

support.note: Moseley, same report: after the advance "did not prove successful", the 21st Virginia fell back about 8 o'clock to the branch at the foot of the mountain. This is the end of its first attack, not the start.

support.quote: About 8 p. m. the enemy appeared on our right flank

witness.name: George S. Greene
witness.role: Brigadier General, commanding the Third Brigade, 2nd Division, XII Corps (alone on Culp's Hill)

support.note: Greene, report of 12 July 1863: about 8 p. m. the enemy appeared on his right flank in the intrenchments Williams's division had left and attacked the right of the 137th New York. A later phase of the same fight, after four charges on the front.

weighing.summary: Greene, who was attacked, gives the one clock reading: "a few minutes before 7 p. m." (report of 12 July). Geary, marching away, has his orders to leave at 7 p. m. (the First Division had gone nearly half an hour before), his column shelled on the way, an order at 7.30 to hold the creek, and Greene attacked "in the meantime": a Union order of events that puts the attack after 19:00 and perhaps after 19:30, the strongest ground for keeping 19:30 selectable. The Confederate reports give an advance about 6 (Moseley) after pickets were relieved at 5 (Steuart), the guns stopping just before sundown and the attack about dusk (Ewell), and darkness in the woods on the climb (Jones). Dusk and dark are periods, and by the computed sunset (19:32) they begin half an hour after Greene's reading; the armies' clocks reportedly differed by about 20 minutes and the Confederate approach took an hour, so the spread of 19:00 to dusk is explained by clock, period and approach, not a flat disagreement. The default is Greene's 19:00, weighted, documented by one witness; 19:30 and 20:00 stay selectable (20:00 has no source for a start).
weighing.who: Greene commanded the brigade that was attacked and was on the spot; Geary and Ewell were away from the point of attack (Geary with two brigades at the turnpike bridge, Ewell behind the Confederate line); Jones led a brigade in the climb; Moseley and Steuart were with their regiment and brigade in the advance.
weighing.when: Greene wrote ten days after (best class); Moseley 19 days; Geary 27; Jones 85; Ewell's report is undated in the print, year 1863; Steuart's of 2 September 1863 (62 days). Greene's account in Battles and Leaders (1887) is later and has the corps leaving "about 7" and the attack just after, a little later than his report. Reports of the time outrank it.
weighing.where: Greene saw the attack arrive on his own line; Moseley and Steuart saw the advance start; Johnson led it; Geary and Ewell relay.
weighing.how_knew: Greene, Moseley, Steuart and Jones knew by being there; Geary by being told; Ewell by report. Only Greene and Geary give a clock reading near the attack; Moseley's and Steuart's hours date the approach.
weighing.clock: Union writers use the army's clock, Confederate writers theirs; the reported difference of about 20 minutes is not applied. It is a possible reason Greene's reading is earlier than the Confederates' dusk. "A few minutes before 7" is read as at or before 19:00; "about 6" as 18:00 plus or minus 15 minutes.
weighing.independence: 19:00 rests on one witness (Greene: his report and his later article are one man; Geary's two and a half hours is only a duration, counted as corroboration of the 7 to 9.30 span, not of 19:00), so it is flagged single-source. 19:30 rests on Geary and Ewell, who do not state it. Dusk and the darkness in the woods are Ewell and Jones; the advance about 6 rests on Moseley alone; Steuart puts his own brigade's move shortly after 5, a different brigade and a different count. No two groups give the same clock reading for the attack.

source_panel_text: About 19:00 on Jul 2: General Greene, whose brigade was attacked on Culp's Hill, wrote ten days later that the attack came a few minutes before 7 p. m. Confederate reports give an advance about 6 and the attack about dusk, which began about half an hour later; no source gives 20:00 for the start. Five other values are listed.

pdf_default.note: 19:00 holds as Greene's reading, the only clock time by a man who was attacked, but on one witness and with hedge (a few minutes before 7); the plan's timeline row marks it documented on web sources, here it rests on an official report.

first_delegated.note: 19:00 (Greene) holds. The first pass's about 18:00 (Moseley) is the advance, not the attack on the works; Ewell's "about dusk" is a period and is carried as its own value.

readers.note: Row "Jul 2 ~19:00 to 19:30": attack begins about 19:00 (Wikipedia/NPS), 19:30 (EPP), dusk; NPS section 11 gives 20:00, tier documented on web leads. Under this resolution 19:00 is Greene's own reading (a few minutes before 7 p. m.), 19:30 and dusk are inferred or periods, and 20:00 has no source for the start (8 o'clock is Moseley's fall-back and the flank attack on Greene); the row's window and sources must follow.

Row "Jul 2 ~19:00, sun ~4.5 deg": Ewell's main assault, three brigades cross Rock Creek and climb the east slope: consistent with the default 19:00 for the contact and with Moseley's advance about 18:00 for the crossing; unchanged.
Row "Jul 2 ~18:30": Greene's brigade alone after the departure of Geary and Kane: matches Greene's 6.30 p. m.; unchanged.
Row "Jul 2 ~18:00": the Twelfth Corps brigades ordered away (1st and 2nd Brigades at 18:30): matches Greene (6.30) and Geary (7 p. m. orders, the First Division gone half an hour earlier); unchanged.
The arrivals rows of Ewell's corps and Johnson's division carry C-019 as a topic cell; their gates are the printed arrival clocks of Jul 1 (14:30 and 19:00), and do not read the attack hour of Jul 2.
As above: the corps's arrival gate (Jul 1 14:30) does not read this value.

what_would_change_it: A report, diary or signal message of 1863 that gives a clock reading for the first charge on Greene's works (Kane's, Ireland's or Cobham's papers, the Twelfth Corps's headquarters log) or a Confederate regiment's report with an hour for crossing Rock Creek would narrow or move the default. Evidence that Greene's watch ran ahead, or an hour for the end of Latimer's artillery fire, would move it toward 19:30.
